Package com.nexuslink.core.security

Class UriRedactor

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.core.security.UriRedactor
public final class UriRedactor extends Object
Hides the credentials inside a connection string, and shortens it to something that fits on one line, for the places a connection is displayed rather than edited.

Connection strings routinely carry a password in plain sight — mongodb://app:s3cret@host/db, redis://:pw@host, amqp://user:pw@broker, jdbc:postgresql://host/db?password=pw. A toolbar that shows one in full puts that password on every screenshot, screen share and shoulder-surf, which is a strange thing for a tool that has a secret vault. Redacting it costs nothing: the value is still there to edit, it is simply not on display until asked for.

Pure and dependency-free, so every scheme's masking is unit-testable.

  • Method Details

    • redact

      public static String redact(String uri)
      The connection string with any embedded credentials masked. Everything else — scheme, hosts, path, options — is left exactly as it was, because that is the part that tells you which server you are looking at.

    • carriesCredentials

      public static boolean carriesCredentials(String uri)
      true when the string carries a credential that redact(java.lang.String) would hide.

    • shortLabel

      public static String shortLabel(String uri)
      A short label for a connection: the host (and database, where the URI names one), with the credentials gone — db.internal:5432/orders rather than the whole string.

      Falls back to the redacted string when the shape is not recognised, because a slightly long label is better than a wrong one.

    • displayName

      public static String displayName(String name, String uri)
      A display name for a connection: the caller's own name when it has one, otherwise shortLabel(java.lang.String). This is what a collapsed connection chip shows.
